symbols.name: W
symbols.def: \(W=(G,Y_0,\ldots,Y_T)\), with untreated outcomes observed only before adoption and realized outcomes observed thereafter

symbols.name: P_W
symbols.space: probability laws on the support of \(W\)

symbols.name: \mathcal U
symbols.space: \(\mathcal U=(u_1,\ldots,u_K)\in(\mathcal Y^{\le K-1})^K\) with distinct entries and \(u_1=\epsilon\)

symbols.name: H_a
symbols.type: shifted predeclared stopped-Hankel minor for \(a\in\mathcal Y\)

symbols.name: \pi^0_{g,r}
symbols.type: untreated cohort path law at lag \(r\)

symbols.name: \mu^1_{g,r}
symbols.type: observed treated cohort mean at lag \(r\)
symbols.def: \(\mu^1_{g,r}=\mathbb E_{P_W}\{W^Y_{g+r}\mid G=g\}\), where \(W^Y_t\) is the outcome coordinate of \(W\)

symbols.name: \mathcal D_{K-1}
symbols.def: canonically ordered monomials in \(\{\bar B_a:a\in\mathcal Y\}\) of total degree at most \(K-1\), including \(I_K\)

symbols.name: q
symbols.type: dimension of the fixed moment vector

symbols.name: m
symbols.role: all word, cohort, and treated-outcome moments used by the fixed chart and target grid

symbols.name: f
symbols.type: total Borel guarded fixed-chart ATT map

symbols.name: \widehat{\bar h}
symbols.def: the canonical adoption terminal obtained from \(\widehat m\) when \(\sigma_{\min}(H(\widehat m))>\kappa_H/2\), and the zero column otherwise

symbols.name: \widehat{\bar v}
symbols.def: the canonical risk terminal obtained from \(\widehat m\) when \(\sigma_{\min}(H(\widehat m))>\kappa_H/2\), and the zero column otherwise

symbols.name: \widehat{\bar B}_a
symbols.type: empirical canonical emission multiplier for \(a\in\mathcal Y\)
symbols.def: the canonical emission multiplier obtained from \(\widehat m\) after the Hankel and killed-transition half-gap gates, and the zero matrix otherwise

symbols.name: \widehat c
symbols.def: \(\widehat c=(\widehat V_F^{\top}\widehat V_F)^{-1}\widehat V_F^{\top}\widehat{\bar h}\) when \(\sigma_{\min}(\widehat V_F)>\kappa_F/2\), and \(\widehat c=0\) otherwise

symbols.name: \widehat\theta
symbols.def: \(\widehat\theta=f(\widehat m)\), with \(f\) defined by the guarded plug-in and fallback rule

symbols.name: d
symbols.type: dimension of the predeclared polynomial frame

symbols.name: \mathcal L_{\mathrm{legal}}
symbols.type: set of legal hazard lifts in the fixed observable realization

symbols.name: \mathfrak W_{2/185}
symbols.type: exact positive three-state, six-date same-observed-law fiber

symbols.name: \mathscr D_{\mathrm{KL}}
symbols.type: Kim--Lee six-period Netflix--IPTV panel with binary VoD outcome

symbols.name: \mathfrak H_{\mathrm{lift}}
symbols.role: two-state alias-block centralizer parameterization, branchwise rational invariants, and subresultant plus Sturm--Habicht component analysis

symbols.name: \mathfrak H_{\mathrm{KL}}
symbols.role: fixed \(K=3\) chart, fixed frame, HDK residual, separation, cohort support, and influence-precision diagnostics

symbols.name: P_{W,N}^{(0)}
symbols.type: first one-panel law on the local collision path
symbols.def: the \(T=5\) stopped-panel law induced by \(\alpha_{\star},P_{\star},h_N^{(0)},B_{0,N}^{\star},B_{1,N}^{\star}\) and the common deterministic treated-outcome law

symbols.name: P_{W,N}^{(1)}
symbols.type: second one-panel law on the local collision path
symbols.def: the \(T=5\) stopped-panel law induced by \(\alpha_N^{(1)},P_N^{(1)},h_N^{(1)},B_{0,N}^{\star},B_{1,N}^{\star}\) and the common deterministic treated-outcome law

symbols.name: \mathfrak C_N
symbols.type: ordered pair of legal local collision laws

symbols.name: \widehat H
symbols.def: the predeclared minor \(H_{\mathcal U,\mathcal V}\) evaluated at \(\widehat m\)

symbols.name: \widehat{\bar K}_0
symbols.def: the canonical killed transition evaluated after the Hankel half-gap gate, and the zero matrix otherwise

symbols.name: \widehat\Sigma
symbols.def: the empirical covariance of the estimated panel-level influence vectors on the guarded inverse branch and \(I_{|\mathcal G|}\) on the fallback branch

symbols.name: \widehat\Pi_F
symbols.def: \(\widehat\Pi_F=\widehat V_F\widehat V_F^{+}\), where the Moore--Penrose inverse makes the projector a total Borel function

symbols.name: \omega_{\max}
symbols.type: fixed maximum acceptable simultaneous ATT half-width

symbols.name: \widehat q_{\mathrm{cert}}
symbols.def: the conditional \(1-\alpha_{\mathrm{cert}}\) quantile of the maximum studentized panel-multiplier perturbation over all preregistered diagnostic and ATT coordinates on the guarded branch, and the fixed value \(1\) on the fallback branch

symbols.name: \widehat{\operatorname{se}}
symbols.sig: a scalar diagnostic or ATT coordinate \(a\mapsto\widehat{\operatorname{se}}(a)\)
symbols.def: the plug-in standard error on the guarded branch and the fixed value \(1\) for every coordinate on the fallback branch

symbols.name: \mathcal C_{\mathrm{KL}}
symbols.role: one preregistered stratum passes all simultaneous rank, HDK, conditioning, support, gray-zone, and precision gates

assumptions.condition: \(W_1,\ldots,W_N\) are independent and identically distributed with law \(P_W\).
For every \(t\), the observed outcome equals \(Y_t(G)\).
The law of \(((S_t),(Y_t(\infty)))\) factors with initial row \(\alpha\), time-homogeneous transition \(P\), and time-homogeneous emissions \(\{B_a:a\in\mathcal Y\}\).
Conditional on \(S_t\) and survival to \(t\), adoption at \(t\) is Bernoulli with mean \(h_{S_t}\).

novel.justification: The condition models adoption as a decision driven by the current latent behavioral regime, as when subscription propensity responds to a household's current engagement state.

assumptions.condition: Conditional on \(S_t\) and survival to \(t\), adoption at \(t\) is independent of \(Y_t(\infty)\) and all future untreated transition and emission innovations.

novel.justification: A fresh subscription decision may depend on the current engagement regime without foreknowledge of future viewing shocks. This structural timing condition is plausible when future content and idiosyncratic viewing innovations have not yet been realized.
The horizon ties observable history length to a known finite predictive order. For \(K=3\), a six-date panel such as the Kim--Lee application supplies exactly the required window.

assumptions.condition: There is a fixed \(\varepsilon_h>0\) such that \(\varepsilon_h\le h_s\le1-\varepsilon_h\) for every hidden state \(s\).
The full finite two-terminal stopped Hankel array with prefix and suffix words \(u,w\in\mathcal Y^{\le K-1}\), terminal labels \(b\in\{R,A\}\), and entries \(F_b(uw)\) has rank \(K\).

novel.justification: This tailored stopped-law realization condition concerns the full paired risk-and-adoption Hankel array. Every entry is an observable stopped-word probability, and rank \(K\) guarantees that some \(K\times K\) minor is nonsingular. It does not guarantee that the particular tuple \(\mathcal U,\mathcal V\) fixed before observing outcomes selects such a minor; that separate requirement is directly auditable from its observable entries.

This preregistered selected-minor condition makes the displayed coordinates reproducible: the ordered word tuples are fixed before outcomes are inspected, and the determinant is an observable polynomial in stopped-word probabilities. Full predictive rank ensures that some minor works but does not privilege this declared one.

assumptions.condition: The frontier support tuple is \((K,T,\mathcal Y)=(3,5,\{0,1\})\).

novel.justification: This fixed finite instance is the smallest six-date binary configuration that contains a two-state alias block and a distinct state while matching the named empirical horizon.

assumptions.condition: After one latent permutation, states \(1\) and \(2\) have identical emission profiles, while state \(3\) has a different emission profile.

novel.justification: The condition isolates the empirically relevant case of two behavioral substates with the same current binary response and one observably distinct regime; it is the exact non-generic geometry the frontier question classifies.

assumptions.condition: Every entry of \(\alpha\) and \(P\), every emission probability, and every component of \(h\) and \(1-h\) is strictly positive.

novel.justification: Strictly positive latent transitions, binary response probabilities, and adoption hazards describe panels without structural zeros and keep the frontier focused on alias geometry rather than boundary support failures.

standard.name: Full-rank transition condition for observable operators

assumptions.condition: For all hidden states \(s,s'\), if \(B_a(s,s)=B_a(s',s')\) for every \(a\in\mathcal Y\), then \(h_s=h_{s'}\).

novel.justification: The restriction says that observationally indistinguishable current regimes have the same adoption propensity. It holds when adoption responds to the current observable engagement profile rather than to distinctions that have no contemporaneous behavioral manifestation.

This custom declared-chart condition requires the particular observable Hankel minor used by the estimator to remain stably invertible. Its empirical audit is the simultaneous lower confidence bound for \(\sigma_{\min}(H)\) against the preregistered threshold \(\kappa_H\).

This custom de-killing condition keeps inversion of the canonical killed dynamics stable in the declared coordinates. Its empirical audit compares a simultaneous lower confidence bound for \(\sigma_{\min}(\bar K_0)\) with \(\kappa_0\).

This custom coefficient-normalized frame condition stabilizes the hazard-algebra Gram solve for the exact written-order dictionary. Its empirical audit compares a simultaneous lower confidence bound for \(\sigma_{\min}(V_F)\) with \(\kappa_F\).

A predeclared low-degree frame records which current emission profiles are empirically distinguishable. Repeated emissions generate a stable lower-dimensional frame in finite-alphabet panels, including binary engagement panels with latent behavioral substates.

definitions.name: Ambient stopped-HMM class \(\mathcal M^{\mathrm{stop}}_{K,T}\)
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal M^{\mathrm{stop}}_{K,T}=\{P_W:P_W\text{ satisfies the listed causal, homogeneous finite-HMM, overlap, predictive-rank, killed-inverse, and cohort-support properties for the displayed }K,T\}\).

definitions.name: Hazard-lift panel class \(\mathcal M^{\mathrm{HL}}_{K,T}\)
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal M^{\mathrm{HL}}_{K,T}=\{P_W\in\mathcal M^{\mathrm{stop}}_{K,T}:P_W\text{ satisfies the within-emission-profile hazard property}\}\).

definitions.name: Predeclared-chart subclass \(\mathcal M^{\mathrm{HL}}_{K,T}(\mathcal U,\mathcal V)\)
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal M^{\mathrm{HL}}_{K,T}(\mathcal U,\mathcal V)=\{P_W\in\mathcal M^{\mathrm{HL}}_{K,T}:\det H_{\mathcal U,\mathcal V}(P_W)\ne0\}\) for the ordered tuples \(\mathcal U=(u_1,\ldots,u_K)\) and \(\mathcal V=((w_1,b_1),\ldots,(w_K,b_K))\) fixed before outcomes are observed, with \(u_1=\epsilon\).

definitions.name: Positive one-alias-block stratum \(\mathcal S^{+}_{2+1}\)
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal S^{+}_{2+1}=\{P_W\in\mathcal M^{\mathrm{stop}}_{K,T}:K=3,\ T=5,\ \mathcal Y=\{0,1\},\ \det H_{\mathcal U,\mathcal V}\ne0,\text{ the emission partition has blocks }\{1,2\},\{3\},\text{ and all primitive probabilities are interior}\}\).

definitions.name: Stopped word probabilities
definitions.construction: For a word \(w=(a_1,\ldots,a_\ell)\), set \(M_w=M_{a_1}\cdots M_{a_\ell}\), \(F_R(w)=\alpha M_wv\), and \(F_A(w)=\alpha M_wh\); these probabilities are coordinates of \(P_W\).

definitions.name: Predeclared-minor canonical stopped-law realization
definitions.construction: For \(\mathcal U=(u_1,\ldots,u_K)\) with \(u_1=\epsilon\) and \(\mathcal V=((w_1,b_1),\ldots,(w_K,b_K))\), set \(H_{\mathcal U,\mathcal V}[i,j]=F_{b_j}(u_iw_j)\) and \(H_a[i,j]=F_{b_j}(u_i a w_j)\). On \(\mathcal M^{\mathrm{HL}}_{K,T}(\mathcal U,\mathcal V)\), set \(\bar M_a=H_{\mathcal U,\mathcal V}^{-1}H_a\), \(\bar\alpha\) equal to the empty-prefix coordinate row, \(\bar v=H_{\mathcal U,\mathcal V}^{-1}f_R\), and \(\bar h=H_{\mathcal U,\mathcal V}^{-1}f_A\), where \(f_R,f_A\) are the corresponding risk and adoption terminal columns.

definitions.name: Hazard-lift operator
definitions.construction: Let \(\operatorname{ev}_{\bar v}(A)=A\bar v\) for \(A\in\mathcal A_O\). Set \(L=\operatorname{ev}_{\bar v}^{-1}(\bar h)\) and \(P_{\mathrm{dk}}=(I_K-L)^{-1}\bar K_0\).

definitions.name: Hazard-lift cohort functional
definitions.construction: For \(z_0,\ldots,z_r\in\mathcal Y\), define \(\pi^0_{g,r}(z_0,\ldots,z_r)=\bar\alpha\bar K_0^gL\bar B_{z_0}P_{\mathrm{dk}}\bar B_{z_1}\cdots P_{\mathrm{dk}}\bar B_{z_r}\bar v/p_g\), and define \(\mu^0_{g,r}=\bar\alpha\bar K_0^gLP_{\mathrm{dk}}^rE\bar v/p_g\).

definitions.name: Legal hazard-lift fiber
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal L_{\mathrm{legal}}\) is the set of matrices \(J\) for which some invertible change of coordinates makes \(\bar v\) the all-ones vector, every \(\bar B_a\) a nonnegative emission diagonal summing to \(I_K\), \(J\) an interior diagonal hazard, \(\bar\alpha\) a probability row, \((I_K-J)^{-1}\bar K_0\) a nonnegative stochastic matrix, and \(J\bar v=\bar h\).

definitions.name: Exact positive three-state negative fiber \(\mathfrak W_{2/185}\)
definitions.construction: Set \(K=3\), \(T=5\), \(g=0\), \(r=1\), \(\mathcal Y=\{0,1\}\), \(\alpha=(3/10,4/10,3/10)\), emission means \((1/5,1/5,4/5)\), \(P=((3/5,3/10,1/10),(1/5,1/2,3/10),(1/10,1/5,7/10))\), \(h=(1/10,3/10,9/20)\), and \(S_{\star}=((9/10,1/10,0),(1/10,9/10,0),(0,0,1))\). The second realization is obtained by \(\alpha'=\alpha S_{\star}\), \(K_0'=S_{\star}^{-1}K_0S_{\star}\), \(h'=S_{\star}^{-1}h\), unchanged emissions, and \(P'=(I_3-\operatorname{diag}(h'))^{-1}K_0'\). The two laws are restricted to the same six observed dates \(0,\ldots,5\), and every treated outcome is the same fixed constant in both realizations.

definitions.name: Declared regular chart stratum \(\mathcal P_{\kappa}\)
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal P_{\kappa}=\{P_W\in\mathcal M^{\mathrm{HL}}_{K,T}(\mathcal U,\mathcal V):\sigma_{\min}(H_{\mathcal U,\mathcal V})\ge\kappa_H,\ \sigma_{\min}(\bar K_0)\ge\kappa_0,\ \sigma_{\min}(V_F)\ge\kappa_F,\ \operatorname{span}(V_F)=\operatorname{span}(V_D),\ \min_{(g,r)\in\mathcal G}p_g\ge\kappa_p,\ \min_j\Sigma_{jj}\ge\kappa_V\}\).

definitions.name: Total guarded fixed-frame plug-in estimator
definitions.construction: Fix \(\theta^{\circ}\) before sampling. From \(\widehat m\), first form the polynomial matrix \(\widehat H\) and continue only if \(\sigma_{\min}(\widehat H)>\kappa_H/2\). On that branch compute the canonical realization and \(\widehat{\bar K}_0\), continuing only if \(\sigma_{\min}(\widehat{\bar K}_0)>\kappa_0/2\). Next compute \(\widehat{\bar B}_a\) and \(\widehat V_F\), continuing only if \(\sigma_{\min}(\widehat V_F)>\kappa_F/2\). Then form \(\widehat c\) and \(\widehat L\), continuing only if \(\sigma_{\min}(I_K-\widehat L)>\tau_N\), \(\min_{(g,r)\in\mathcal G}\widehat p_g>\kappa_p/2\), every other inverse not protected by a declared fixed gap has smallest singular value greater than \(\tau_N\), every remaining scalar denominator in the ATT and influence formulas has absolute value greater than \(\tau_N\), and the computed marginal influence variances exceed \(\kappa_V/2\). On the final pass branch, evaluate the ATT, covariance, studentization, and multiplier critical value by their displayed plug-in formulas. At the first failed gate, return \(\widehat\theta=\theta^{\circ}\), \(\widehat\Sigma=I_{|\mathcal G|}\), unit standard errors, and critical value \(1\). Ties take the fallback branch. This sequential piecewise rule is a total Borel map \(f\).

definitions.name: Algebra-collision gray zone
definitions.construction: For a predeclared frame of dimension \(d<K\), set \(\rho_N=c_{\rho}\sqrt{\log N/N}\) and \(s_{d+1}(m)=\sigma_{d+1}(V_D(m))\). Define \(\mathcal Z_{\mathrm{gray},N}=\{m:0<s_{d+1}(m)\le\rho_N\}\cup\{m:\rho_N<s_{d+1}(m)<\kappa_{\mathrm{gap}}\}\). The first component is the sampling-noise collision band and the second is the weakly separated band; exact rank-\(d\) laws with \(s_{d+1}(m)=0\) and laws with \(s_{d+1}(m)\ge\kappa_{\mathrm{gap}}\) are outside this population gray zone. For \(d=K\), set \(\mathcal Z_{\mathrm{gray},N}=\varnothing\).

definitions.name: Explicit legal collision path \(\mathfrak C_N\)
definitions.construction: Fix \(K=3\), \(T=5\), \(g=0\), and \(r=1\). For all sufficiently large \(N\), evaluate the explicitly declared \(\eta_N=N^{-1/4}\), \(\zeta_N=N^{-1}\), base parameters \(\alpha_{\star},P_{\star},S_{\star}\), hazards \(h_N^{(0)},h_N^{(1)}\), emissions \(B_{0,N}^{\star},B_{1,N}^{\star}\), and transformed transition \(P_N^{(1)}\). These parameters induce the two six-date stopped-panel laws \(P_{W,N}^{(0)}\) and \(P_{W,N}^{(1)}\) with the same deterministic treated-outcome law. Set \(\mathfrak C_N=(P_{W,N}^{(0)},P_{W,N}^{(1)})\), and evaluate its target only at \(\mu^0_{0,1}\) and \(\tau_{0,1}\).

definitions.name: Fixed one-alias-block legal-lift stratification handle
definitions.construction: Restrict to \(\mathcal S^{+}_{2+1}\), fix \((g,r)=(0,1)\), and use \(\mathfrak H_{\mathrm{lift}}\) as follows. Form the similarity-invariant projector onto the emission-distinct state and its complementary two-state alias block from rational fixed-chart stopped-law coordinates. Parameterize the legal similarity centralizer on that two-state block, clear only denominators certified nonzero on the positive interior stratum, and reduce constancy of each coordinate of \(\pi^0_{0,1}\) to branchwise univariate numerator tests. Use subresultant chains and Sturm--Habicht sign determination to enumerate all positive legal-fiber components, separating the HDK branch from each forecast-degenerate numerator branch on which HDK fails but \(\pi^0_{0,1}\) is constant. Record every resulting polynomial or rational invariant and its degree; exploit the fixed one-block dimension rather than generic cylindrical algebraic decomposition.
inputs: rational coordinates of \(P_W\in\mathcal S^{+}_{2+1}\) in the predeclared chart

definitions.name: Kim--Lee empirical-certificate handle
definitions.construction: For each preregistered observable stratum of \(\mathscr D_{\mathrm{KL}}\), use the fixed \(K=3\) chart and frame and compute \(\widehat R_{\mathrm{HDK}}=\|(I_3-\widehat\Pi_F)\widehat{\bar h}\|_2\). One panel-level Gaussian multiplier bootstrap jointly perturbs \(\widehat m\), recomputes every diagnostic and \(\widehat\theta\), and returns the common \(1-\alpha_{\mathrm{cert}}\) maximum-statistic critical value \(\widehat q_{\mathrm{cert}}\) and endpoints \(\operatorname{LCB}_N,\operatorname{UCB}_N\). Declare \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{KL}}\) to occur only if, for at least one stratum, \(\operatorname{LCB}_N(\sigma_3(\widehat H))\ge\kappa_H\), \(\operatorname{LCB}_N(\sigma_3(\widehat{\bar K}_0))\ge\kappa_0\), \(\operatorname{LCB}_N(\sigma_d(\widehat V_F))\ge\kappa_F\), \(\operatorname{LCB}_N(\min_{(g,r)\in\mathcal G}\widehat p_g)\ge\kappa_p\), \(\operatorname{LCB}_N(\min_j\widehat\Sigma_{jj})\ge\kappa_V\), and \(\operatorname{UCB}_N(\widehat R_{\mathrm{HDK}})\le\varepsilon_{\mathrm{HDK}}\); the simultaneous interval for \(\sigma_{d+1}(\widehat V_D)\) is disjoint from \((0,\kappa_{\mathrm{gap}})\) when \(d<3\); and \(\widehat\omega_{\max}\le\omega_{\max}\). All constants, strata, chart, frame, grid, and the convention that no omitted singular value is tested when \(d=3\) are fixed before inspecting outcomes.

statements.statement: Under \(T\ge2K-1\), rank \(K\) of the full two-terminal stopped Hankel array implies that the stopped series has a minimal \(K\)-dimensional linear realization, and any two minimal realizations are related by one common invertible similarity. Predictive rank guarantees that some \(K\times K\) minor is nonsingular but does not guarantee the preregistered minor \(H_{\mathcal U,\mathcal V}\). If \(P_W\in\mathcal M^{\mathrm{HL}}_{K,T}(\mathcal U,\mathcal V)\), the fixed \(H_{\mathcal U,\mathcal V}^{-1}\) formulas recover the displayed realization from stopped words of length at most \(2K-1\).
statements.justification: This separates chart-independent minimal realization from the extra preregistered-minor condition needed for reproducible inverse coordinates.
statements.gap: Hsu, Kakade, and Zhang give observable operators for an ordinary HMM, while Weiss and Nadler analyze alias similarities. Neither paper states the tailored two-terminal stopped Hankel rank condition or constructs the risk-and-adoption chart used here.
statements.consumer: The theorem supplies finite observable inputs from a six-date binary panel when \(K=3\), provided the declared minor rather than an outcome-selected minor is nonsingular.

statements.statement: For every \(P_W\in\mathcal M^{\mathrm{HL}}_{K,T}\), any valid stopped-Hankel chart yields an equation \(L\bar v=\bar h\) with a unique solution in \(\mathcal A_O\). For every \((g,r)\in\mathcal G\), the resulting \(\pi^0_{g,r}\) equals the conditional law of \((Y_g(\infty),\ldots,Y_{g+r}(\infty))\) given \(G=g\), is invariant over the choice of valid chart and all legal non-permutation aliased realizations, and identifies \(\tau_{g,r}\). On \(\mathcal M^{\mathrm{HL}}_{K,T}(\mathcal U,\mathcal V)\), this invariant is evaluated by the displayed predeclared-coordinate formulas.
statements.justification: The result identifies an entire cohort counterfactual law even when the latent transition and initial distribution are not identified.
statements.gap: Weiss and Nadler characterize aliased parameter fibers, and Ishimaru identifies ATT by repeated measurements outside evolving staggered selection. Pennoni, Paas, and Bartolucci use propensity-weighted latent-state likelihood, while Clouth, Bijlsma, Pauws, and Vermunt use a fitted latent Markov measurement model inside the parametric g-formula. None provides a stopped-law hazard operator or proves causal functional invariance on a legal non-permutation alias fiber.
statements.consumer: Kim and Lee's binary VoD panel can replace observed-history extrapolation by a latent-state selection correction whenever the observable certificate passes.

statements.statement: Suppose a legal realization has strictly positive \(\alpha\) and \(P\), interior hazards and emissions, and two states \(i,j\) with identical emission profiles. If \(h_i\ne h_j\) and \((Pe)_i\ne(Pe)_j\), then a relatively open neighborhood within the aliased model contains a continuum of legal non-permutation realizations with the same complete observed stopped-panel law and different \(\mu^0_{g,1}\) for every supported cohort \(g\). Along the alias-preserving direction, the derivative is \((\alpha K_0^g)_i(h_j-h_i)((Pe)_j-(Pe)_i)/\{(1-h_i)p_g\}\).
statements.justification: The converse diagnoses attempts to transport a weighted-HMM or latent-Markov parametric g-formula workflow to stopped panels while requiring continuation to be determined by the observed stopped law.
statements.gap: Pennoni, Paas, and Bartolucci and Clouth, Bijlsma, Pauws, and Vermunt impose their own propensity, exchangeability, measurement, and structural-model conditions. This theorem does not contradict those procedures; it shows that without an additional restriction, unequal within-alias hazards and forecasts prevent a unique observed-stopped-law continuation.
statements.consumer: A transported fitted-latent-state workflow receives a precise warning: on an alias block, observed-stopped-law-determined continuation requires an extra restriction unless the forecast contrast is degenerate.

statements.statement: On the fixed horizon \(T=5\), the construction \(\mathfrak W_{2/185}\) consists of two strictly positive stochastic three-state realizations with \(p_0>0\), full predictive rank, and invertible killed dynamics. The two realizations generate exactly the same probabilities for every stopped word observable on dates \(0,\ldots,5\) and the same post-adoption outcomes. At the fixed cohort \(g=0\), \(\mu^0_{0,0}=46/95\) in both realizations, whereas \(\mu^0_{0,1}=457/950\) and \((\mu^0_{0,1})'=17289/35150\), so \((\mu^0_{0,1})'-\mu^0_{0,1}=2/185\). With their common constant treated outcome, \((\tau_{0,1})'-\tau_{0,1}=-2/185\).
statements.justification: The exact pair is a stress test for transported fitted-latent-state workflows and observed-history matching under unmodeled evolving hidden selection.
statements.gap: All stopped-panel observables agree while the fixed \(T=5\), \(g=0\), \(r=1\) ATT coordinate differs. This necessitates an extra restriction but does not contradict Pennoni, Paas, and Bartolucci, Clouth, Bijlsma, Pauws, and Vermunt, Kim and Lee, or Ishimaru because their identifying conditions are not asserted on this pair.
statements.consumer: The rational pair is a reproducible stress test: any transported latent-state fit or Kim--Lee-style observed-history match must expose which extra restriction selects one of its two \(\tau_{0,1}\) values.

statements.statement: If \(K=1\), write \(b_a=\Pr(Y_t(\infty)=a)\) and let \(h\) be the scalar hazard. Then \(P=1\), \(K_0=1-h\), \(p_g=(1-h)^gh\), \(L=h\), \(P_{\mathrm{dk}}=1\), \(\pi^0_{g,r}(z_0,\ldots,z_r)=\prod_{j=0}^r b_{z_j}\), and \(\mu^0_{g,r}=\sum_{a\in\mathcal Y}\nu(a)b_a\). If the \(K\) emission-profile vectors \(\{(B_a(s,s):a\in\mathcal Y):1\le s\le K\}\) are pairwise distinct, multivariate polynomial interpolation gives every diagonal matrix in the latent-coordinate emission algebra; hence the canonical \(L\) is similar to \(D\), \(P_{\mathrm{dk}}\) is similar to \(P\), and the observable formulas reduce exactly to \(\pi^0_{g,r}(z_0,\ldots,z_r)=\alpha K_0^gDB_{z_0}PB_{z_1}\cdots PB_{z_r}v/p_g\) and \(\mu^0_{g,r}=\alpha K_0^gDP^re/p_g\). If \(h_s=\lambda\) for every state, then \(L=\lambda I_K\) and \(P_{\mathrm{dk}}\) is similar to \(P\). For \(r=0\), \(\mu^0_{g,0}=\bar\alpha\bar K_0^gE\bar h/p_g\) without the hazard-algebra restriction.
statements.justification: These reductions prevent the new formula from contradicting ordinary identified HMMs or the mechanically identified contemporaneous cohort mean.
statements.gap: The reductions are sanity checks rather than novelty claims.
statements.consumer: They give implementers diagnostic benchmarks for one-state, distinct-emission, constant-hazard, and contemporaneous-effect cases.

statements.statement: Uniformly over compact subsets of \(\mathcal P_{\kappa}\) satisfying independent-panel sampling and the moment envelope, the guarded estimator takes its inverse-formula branch with probability tending to one, so \(\sqrt N(\widehat\theta-\theta)=N^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^N\varphi(W_i)+o_{P_W}(1)\), and \(\widehat\Sigma\) consistently estimates \(\Sigma\). A panel-level Gaussian multiplier critical value yields asymptotically simultaneous \(1-\alpha_0\) coverage for the fixed grid \(\mathcal G\). The fixed fallback values therefore do not change the regular-subset expansion.
statements.justification: The theorem supplies joint uncertainty for all cohort-time effects while retaining covariance between observed treated means and reconstructed counterfactuals.
statements.gap: Tran, Kim, and Doshi-Velez motivate a moment-estimation route without proving the custom stopped-chart, killed-inverse, or polynomial-frame gaps used here. Callaway and Sant'Anna begin with regular ATT scores; neither source derives the influence map through hazard lifting and de-killing.
statements.consumer: The fixed-grid band directly supports Kim and Lee's cohort, calendar-time, and exposure-duration heterogeneity contrasts for binary VoD use.

statements.statement: Fix \(K=3\), \(T=5\), and the cohort--lag pair \((g,r)=(0,1)\). Along \(\mathfrak C_N\), both six-date realizations have strictly positive initial probabilities, transitions, emissions, interior hazards, and \(p_0>0\) for all sufficiently large \(N\). Their stopped-word probabilities agree exactly when \(\zeta_N=0\); at the declared \(\zeta_N=N^{-1}\), \(\operatorname{KL}(P_{W,N}^{(0)},P_{W,N}^{(1)})=O(\zeta_N^2)\) and \(\operatorname{KL}((P_{W,N}^{(0)})^{\otimes N},(P_{W,N}^{(1)})^{\otimes N})=O(N\zeta_N^2)=O(N^{-1})\). Under \(P_{W,N}^{(0)}\), the declared canonical matrix with \(d=2\) satisfies \(\sigma_3(V_D)=(10.33271+o(1))\zeta_N\), while \((\mu^0_{0,1})^{(1)}-(\mu^0_{0,1})^{(0)}=63\eta_N/544+o(\eta_N)\); the common deterministic treated outcome gives the opposite gap for \(\tau_{0,1}\). Hence the product-law total variation tends to zero, the \(\tau_{0,1}\) separation is of order \(N^{-1/4}\), this path lies in \(0<\sigma_3(V_D)\le\rho_N\), and for every fixed \(\alpha_0<1/2\) no confidence band for \(\tau_{0,1}\) can have uniform \(1-\alpha_0\) coverage over this pair and diameter \(o(N^{-1/4})\) in probability under both product laws.
statements.justification: This lower bound limits the proposal's own guarded fixed-chart hazard-lift plug-in on the displayed \(T=5\), \(g=0\), \(r=1\) pair.
statements.gap: Andrews and Cheng provide weak-identification precedent. The displayed path is a hazard-lift-specific modulus and does not contradict Tran, Kim, and Doshi-Velez or Callaway and Sant'Anna on their separated regular domains.
statements.consumer: Analysts using this proposal's fixed-chart plug-in receive an explicit gray-zone rule: over the displayed pair, no band combines uniform \(1-\alpha_0\) coverage with \(o(N^{-1/4})\) diameter.

statements.statement: Fix \(K=3\), \(T=5\), \(\mathcal Y=\{0,1\}\), \((g,r)=(0,1)\), and \(P_W\in\mathcal S^{+}_{2+1}\). Using \(\mathfrak H_{\mathrm{lift}}\), derive a finite similarity-invariant observable stratification that determines whether \(\{\pi^0_{0,1}(J):J\in\mathcal L_{\mathrm{legal}}\}\subseteq\Delta^3\) is a singleton. The stratification must separate the HDK branch from every forecast-degenerate branch on which HDK fails but the target remains constant, list explicit polynomial or rational invariants and their degrees, and enumerate every positive legal-fiber component. For rational fixed-chart input, give a terminating algorithm and prove a bit-complexity bound polynomial in the coefficient bit length for this fixed stratum, hence strictly sharper than generic cylindrical algebraic decomposition or quantifier elimination.
statements.justification: The sufficiency theorem and generic converse leave a non-generic, fixed one-alias-block boundary whose observable branch structure is unknown.
statements.gap: Generic semialgebraic decidability and equality over legal lifts merely restate the problem. No located result supplies explicit invariants, degrees, component enumeration, and a fixed-dimension bit bound for this target-active stopped-HMM stratum.
statements.consumer: The stratification would convert HDK rejection into a complete \(K=3\), binary, six-date diagnostic for the first future cohort forecast and would retain forecast-degenerate cases where the target is nevertheless identified.

statements.statement: Using \(\mathfrak H_{\mathrm{KL}}\) with the fixed thresholds and one joint multiplier decision rule in its construction, does the pass event \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{KL}}\) occur for at least one preregistered observable stratum of \(\mathscr D_{\mathrm{KL}}\)?
statements.justification: The fixed familywise gate makes empirical usability, rather than symbolic identification alone, the unresolved kill test for the named six-period consumer.
statements.gap: Kim and Lee report matching and cohort-time diagnostics but not a joint stopped-rank, HDK-residual, de-killing, frame-conditioning, cohort-support, gray-zone, and precision decision with preregistered thresholds.
statements.consumer: A positive certificate would deliver the first directly usable hazard-lift analysis of Netflix adoption; universal rejection or gray-zone classification would honestly kill that application claim.

sampling_model.design: Large-\(N\), fixed-\(T\) observational panel with a predeclared stopped-Hankel chart, polynomial frame, and cohort-time grid.
sampling_model.units: The panels \(W_i\) are independent draws from \(P_W\); within-panel dependence is generated by the untreated hidden Markov law and staggered adoption.
sampling_model.treatment: Adoption is absorbing and occurs with a current-hidden-state hazard before the period's untreated outcome, with fresh adoption randomization conditionally independent of future untreated innovations.
sampling_model.overlap: State hazards are interior and every target cohort has mass bounded away from zero on the inference stratum.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: All nuisance objects are finite stopped-word moments evaluated through one ordered Hankel minor fixed before outcomes and one fixed coefficient-normalized polynomial frame; no empirical latent labeling, rank-revealing minor selection, or adaptive frame search is used. The estimator is a total Borel map with sequential half-gap and uncovered-inverse gates and fixed fallback outputs. The Kim--Lee usability screen jointly bootstraps the same moment vector and applies only preregistered rank, gap, residual, cohort-mass, and ATT-half-width thresholds.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The paper characterizes minimality and observational equivalence for parametric-output HMMs with exactly two aliased states.
Theorem 1 identifies ATT from repeated measurements, while Section 3.3 states that evolving hidden shocks create a staggered-selection failure for that construction.
Theorem 1 identifies group-time ATT under conditional parallel trends and the paper establishes simultaneous multiplier-bootstrap inference.

Under an interactive fixed-effects law for untreated outcomes and adoption-group moment and rank conditions, the main identification theorem recovers group-time ATT from observed cohort moments, with joint asymptotic inference developed in Proposition 1 and the multiplier-bootstrap corollary.
Theorem 6 bounds HMM prediction error under observable singular-value separation.
Proposition 1 represents the spectral HMM estimator as an equivalent moment estimator, and Section 3.4 optimizes its moment weighting.

The paper estimates effects of a dynamic treatment on potential latent-state distributions by inverse-probability-weighted hidden-Markov maximum likelihood under observed-confounder treatment assignment assumptions.

The paper combines a bias-adjusted three-step latent Markov measurement model with a parametric g-formula under exchangeability, positivity, consistency, no interference, and latent-Markov restrictions.
The paper identifies staggered-adoption effects by design-based matching on observed histories under its stated identifying conditions and applies the method to six-period Netflix--IPTV data.
The paper develops estimation and inference across weak, semi-strong, and strong identification sequences.

tldr: State-dependent adoption usually destroys parallel-trends comparisons because future untreated outcomes are missing precisely for selected latent states. A finite stopped-panel law nevertheless identifies every adopter cohort's untreated path law when the adoption hazard is constant within each current-emission alias class. Predictive rank yields a chart-independent minimal realization, while displayed coordinates and inference use one ordered Hankel minor fixed before outcomes and a total guarded estimator with a preregistered fallback. A generic legal fiber proves failure when aliased states have unequal hazards and forecasts; the exact positive \(T=5\), \(g=0\), \(r=1\) witness has ATT gap \(2/185\), and the local collision pair limits this proposal's plug-in at \(N^{-1/4}\). The exceptional \(K=3\) one-alias-block frontier and the Kim--Lee empirical certificate remain first-class open questions.

project_justification.gap: Staggered-DiD and interactive-fixed-effects methods use observed histories or adoption-date cohort moments. Causal latent-Markov procedures impose their own model-based latent recovery and ignorability structures, while HMM identification results either exclude exact aliasing or characterize latent ambiguity rather than observed-stopped-law-determined cohort continuation. Ordinary spectral results also do not select a preregistered stopped-Hankel minor.
project_justification.niche: The adoption event is an observable state-dependent mark. Its terminal vector can identify a similarity-invariant hazard operator even when positive non-permutation latent realizations fit the same stopped law; a fixed ordered minor is needed only to compute coordinates reproducibly, not to define the invariant.
project_justification.fill: The project proves hazard-lift path-law invariance, derives the generic converse and exact \(2/185\) stress test, supplies a total guarded fixed-chart estimator and regular-subset simultaneous inference, limits its own plug-in on an explicit collision path, and isolates both a concrete one-alias-block frontier and an operational empirical certificate as open questions.

related_work: Weiss and Nadler characterize non-permutation equivalence for HMMs with two aliased states; their similarities inform the legal fiber but do not target counterfactual cohort continuation. Allman, Matias, and Rhodes establish generic finite-window identification, while Gassiat, Cleynen, and Robin and Alexandrovich, Holzmann, and Leister use separation conditions that exclude exact repeated emissions. Bartolucci and Farcomeni provide a killed-forward latent event-history model without the proposed causal invariant. Pennoni, Paas, and Bartolucci use propensity-weighted hidden-Markov likelihood, and Clouth, Bijlsma, Pauws, and Vermunt use a fitted latent Markov measurement model inside a parametric g-formula. The generic converse diagnoses transporting those workflows to stopped panels while also demanding that continuation be determined by the observed stopped law: unequal within-alias hazards and forecasts preclude uniqueness absent another restriction. Those papers impose their own structural assumptions and are not contradicted, and the hazard-lift theorem does not identify their latent-state estimands. Callaway and Sant'Anna identify group-time ATT and simultaneous inference under conditional parallel trends. Callaway and Tsyawo use interactive fixed effects and adoption-date moments; their functional has neither a state-dependent stopping mark nor alias-fiber invariance, while hazard lifting does not impose their factor structure. Kim and Lee use observed-history matching in the six-period Netflix--IPTV panel, and Ishimaru uses repeated measurements outside evolving hidden selection. The exact pair is a stress test for transported fitted-state workflows and observed-history matching, not a contradiction of either paper because their assumptions are not asserted on the pair. Hsu, Kakade, and Zhang provide ordinary-HMM observable operators, but full predictive rank only ensures that some minor is nonsingular and does not validate the preregistered minor used here. Tran, Kim, and Doshi-Velez provide a moment-estimation template but not the stopped-chart, de-killing, or frame conditions. Andrews and Cheng provide weak-identification precedent; the collision proposition instead limits this proposal's fixed-chart plug-in and does not contradict the separated regular domains of Tran, Kim, and Doshi-Velez or Callaway and Sant'Anna. These sources are informed-by comparators, not results claimed to be strictly tightened.
technical_internal_limitation: The empirical algebra cannot be generated by exact commutativity or exact repeated eigenvalues after sampling noise perturbs population moments. The estimator therefore uses a fixed written-order polynomial dictionary and least-squares off-model extension. Full stopped-Hankel rank ensures that some \(K\)-minor works but not that the ordered \(H_{\mathcal U,\mathcal V}\) fixed before outcomes does; all Euclidean separation claims are tied to that declared chart and coefficient normalization. The total estimator uses inverse formulas only behind fixed half-gap gates and the uncovered-inverse threshold \(\tau_N=N^{-1/8}\), and otherwise returns fixed defaults. Along \(\eta_N=N^{-1/4}\) and \(\zeta_N=N^{-1}\), the omitted singular value is \((10.33271+o(1))\zeta_N\), the displayed product laws merge in total variation, and \(\tau_{0,1}\) remains separated at order \(N^{-1/4}\).
honest_scope: The point-identification theorem fixes the hidden order and a finite alphabet, uses \(T\ge2K-1\), assumes time-homogeneous untreated dynamics, invertible killed dynamics, positive cohort masses, and sequential hazard randomization. It identifies finite untreated cohort path laws but not latent labels, transitions, or initial probabilities. Predictive rank yields a chart-independent minimal realization and only guarantees existence of some nonsingular minor; the displayed formulas and inference additionally require the predeclared \(H_{\mathcal U,\mathcal V}\). The generic converse concerns future lags. The exact \(2/185\) witness and local lower bound apply only to \(K=3\), \(T=5\), \(g=0\), and \(r=1\). The lower bound limits this proposal's own fixed-chart plug-in and does not challenge comparator methods on their maintained regular domains. The total estimator has fixed fallback outputs, whose probability vanishes only on compact regular subsets. The open legal-lift classification is restricted to the positive interior binary \(K=3\), \(T=5\), one-two-state-alias-block stratum at \((g,r)=(0,1)\); it demands explicit branch invariants and a complexity improvement over generic elimination. The Kim--Lee data are unavailable, so no empirical certificate is claimed. Unknown order, continuous outcomes, approximate homogeneity, sharp tolerance bounds, adaptive chart selection, constrained-model efficiency, and finite-sample remainders remain open.

seed_details.anchor_locator: Theorem 2 and Sections 4.1--4.2 for the similarity family; the Introduction for the aliasing problem and Section 6 for the learning boundary.
seed_details.opportunity: Characterize when the stopped panel law identifies adopter counterfactual path laws even though aliased latent parameters vary on a non-permutation similarity fiber.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace recovery of a unique transition matrix by construction of the similarity-equivariant operator \(L\in\mathcal A_O\) satisfying \(L\bar v=\bar h\), then de-kill through \((I-L)^{-1}\bar K_0\).
seed_details.target_method_search: Searches combining aliased HMMs, state-dependent adoption, stopped laws, counterfactuals, and group-time ATT returned alias-identification papers and outcome-driven-adoption diagnostics, but no causal hazard-lift functional.
seed_details.referee_objection: This is immediate from Weiss and Nadler because all equivalent aliased HMMs are related by similarity.
seed_details.rebuttal: Their similarity fiber moves the state-dependent hazard and the de-killed forecast; constancy of the causal cohort functional requires the new hazard-in-emission-algebra certificate and fails on an explicit positive fiber when that certificate is absent.

seed_details.anchor_locator: Equation (9), Lemma 2, and Theorem 2 for admissible alias-preserving similarity transformations; the Introduction for the non-permutation ambiguity.
seed_details.opportunity: Prove that unequal hazards and unequal one-step forecasts inside an aliased block generically move group-time ATT along a legal same-observed-law path.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Differentiate the causal de-killed forecast along an alias-preserving stochastic similarity path rather than asking whether the latent transition itself is identifiable.
seed_details.target_method_search: The alias-equivalence literature supplies legal similarity directions, but the search found no derivative formula for a cohort counterfactual or an ATT nonidentification region.
seed_details.referee_objection: A single numerical counterexample would be a hand-tuned witness with no general content.
seed_details.rebuttal: The derivative is nonzero under strict positivity, unequal within-alias hazards, and unequal forecasts, producing a relatively open failure region; the rational \(2/185\) fiber is only an exact certificate.

seed_details.anchor_locator: Sections 3.1 and 3.4, especially Proposition 1 and the GMM weighting construction; the Introduction and Section 6 for robustness and misspecification boundaries.
seed_details.opportunity: Derive joint panel-level influence functions and simultaneous bands for the composed stopped-moment, Gram-solve, de-killing, power, and cohort-quotient map.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Differentiate the fixed observable chart and normalized algebra frame through de-killing before stacking cohort-time coordinates, rather than stopping at prediction-moment efficiency.
seed_details.target_method_search: Spectral GMM papers analyze prediction moments, and staggered-DiD papers analyze already-regular ATT scores; no source differentiates their hazard-lift composition.
seed_details.referee_objection: Once identification is written as a finite smooth map, the delta method and multiplier band are routine.
seed_details.rebuttal: The contribution is the explicit chart derivative and honest separation boundary; the generic delta method is presented as supporting inference rather than the paper's sole novelty.

seed_details.anchor_locator: The Introduction and Section 6.1, especially Theorem 6 and its Kruskal-embedding proof for generic finite-window HMM identification.
seed_details.opportunity: On the fixed positive binary \(K=3\), \(T=5\) stratum with one two-state emission-alias block, derive explicit observable branch invariants deciding singleton \(\pi^0_{0,1}\), including every forecast-degenerate non-HDK branch.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Exploit the one-block centralizer to reduce legal fibers to branchwise univariate sign and numerator problems, then enumerate components with subresultants and Sturm--Habicht sequences instead of generic quantifier elimination.
seed_details.target_method_search: Generic HMM identification leaves exceptional varieties unresolved, and no located paper classifies target-specific constancy on the state-dependent-stopping fiber.
seed_details.referee_objection: Constancy over legal lifts is only a tautological restatement, and generic cylindrical algebraic decomposition already decides it.
seed_details.rebuttal: The required solution must expose similarity-invariant rational tests and degrees, separate HDK from every target-constant forecast-degenerate branch, enumerate all positive components, and prove fixed-stratum bit complexity strictly sharper than generic elimination.

seed_details.anchor_locator: Theorem 6 and Section 4.2 for singular-value-dependent error bounds, together with the Introduction and Appendix B perturbation lemmas.
seed_details.opportunity: Use an explicit local collision pair to delimit fixed-chart ATT inference at the sampling-noise boundary; the maximal stabilized shrinking-gap frontier remains open.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Set \(\eta_N=N^{-1/4}\) and \(\zeta_N=N^{-1}\), calculate product-law divergence and the target modulus, and compare the canonical omitted singular value with \(\rho_N=c_{\rho}\sqrt{\log N/N}\).
seed_details.target_method_search: Rank-robust low-rank inference covers linear high-dimensional functionals, while weak-identification theory covers generic drifting experiments; neither gives the nonlinear hazard-lift frontier.
seed_details.referee_objection: This is generic weak identification with the smallest singular value renamed.
seed_details.rebuttal: The relevant strength is a pair of chart and algebra-frame gaps whose effects pass through inverses, a polynomial solve, and a causal quotient; the attainable phase must be derived for that composed target.

seed_details.anchor_locator: Sections 1.1, 2.1--2.3, 3.2, 4.1, and 5 for the six-period cohort-time design, binary VoD outcome, simultaneous inference, and application limits.
seed_details.opportunity: Apply a preregistered familywise decision rule for predictive rank, HDK residual, inverse and frame separation, cohort support, gray-zone exclusion, and ATT half-width in the Netflix--IPTV panel.

seed_details.referee_objection: A diagnostic checklist is an application appendix, not a theorem-level contribution.
seed_details.rebuttal: The common multiplier critical value, fixed pass inequalities, gray-zone rule, and maximum half-width make the gate reproducible, but without access to the data its outcome remains an empirical open question.

literature_map.anchor_inspiration: Weiss and Nadler's block-similarity parameterization supplies the fiber direction, Bartolucci and Farcomeni's state-driven event history supplies the killed recursion, Tran, Kim, and Doshi-Velez supply the finite-moment differentiation template, Callaway and Tsyawo supply the adjacent adoption-date moment route under interactive fixed effects, Pennoni, Paas, and Bartolucci and Clouth, Bijlsma, Pauws, and Vermunt supply model-based causal latent-Markov contrasts, and Kim and Lee supply the cohort-time estimand and six-period binary consumer.

adjacent_threads.settled: Weiss and Nadler characterize minimality and equivalence for exactly two aliased states. Allman, Matias, and Rhodes establish generic finite-window identification, while Gassiat, Cleynen, and Robin and Alexandrovich, Holzmann, and Leister use emission-separation conditions that exclude exact aliasing.
adjacent_threads.unoccupied_pair: None of these sources gives explicit similarity-invariant branch tests for constancy of \(\pi^0_{0,1}\) on the positive binary \(K=3\), six-date, one-alias-block legal fiber.

adjacent_threads.settled: Callaway and Sant'Anna identify and estimate group-time ATT under conditional parallel trends. Callaway and Tsyawo use adoption-date comparison-group moments under an interactive fixed-effects law to identify selected group-time effects without parallel trends. Kim and Lee use observed-history matching, while Shahn diagnoses failure of parallel trends under outcome-driven treatment. Ishimaru identifies ATT using repeated measurements but explicitly notes that staggered selection on evolving hidden shocks violates his cohort construction.
adjacent_threads.unoccupied_pair: The stopped adoption process has not been used as a hazard-marked measurement that recovers cohort counterfactual laws under evolving latent selection.

adjacent_threads.settled: Bartolucci and Farcomeni model an event time through a shared latent Markov state and evaluate the likelihood by killed forward recursions. Pennoni, Paas, and Bartolucci estimate dynamic-treatment effects on latent-state distributions using inverse-probability-weighted hidden-Markov likelihood. Clouth, Bijlsma, Pauws, and Vermunt combine a fitted three-step latent Markov measurement model with the parametric g-formula under exchangeability and structural-model restrictions.
adjacent_threads.unoccupied_pair: These model-based procedures do not use the adoption event as an observable stopping mark or prove that a causal untreated law is invariant when the latent realization itself is nonidentified.

adjacent_threads.settled: Hsu, Kakade, and Zhang give singular-value-sensitive spectral prediction bounds, and Tran, Kim, and Doshi-Velez formulate spectral recovery as GMM. Callaway and Sant'Anna stack regular cohort-time scores for multiplier inference.
adjacent_threads.unoccupied_pair: No adjacent source differentiates the guarded hazard-algebra Gram solve, de-killing inverse, matrix powers, and cohort quotient on one predeclared repeated-emission minor while making the estimator total off its inverse branch.

literature_map.subsumption_check: Weiss and Nadler supply the closest alias-fiber geometry but no causal target. Callaway and Tsyawo's main theorem recovers group-time ATT from adoption-date moments under an interactive fixed-effects law; it has no state-dependent stopping terminal or alias-fiber invariant, while the hazard-lift theorem does not impose their factor structure, so neither subsumes the other. Pennoni, Paas, and Bartolucci use propensity-weighted likelihood for potential latent states, and Clouth, Bijlsma, Pauws, and Vermunt use a fitted latent measurement model inside a parametric g-formula; neither establishes observable stopped-law invariance over non-permutation alias fibers, while the hazard-lift theorem does not identify their latent-state causal contrasts. Ishimaru's Theorem 1 uses a repeated-measurement decomposition and Section 3.3 excludes staggered cohorts selected by evolving hidden shocks.

literature_checklist.author: Felix J. Clouth, Maarten J. Bijlsma, Steffen Pauws, and Jeroen K. Vermunt
literature_checklist.one_line: The paper combines bias-adjusted three-step latent-state measurement with the parametric g-formula under exchangeability and model restrictions, not state-dependent stopping or alias-fiber invariance.
